questions.stem: In Practice Exam (Topic 5), the metabolic cell body of a neurone containing the nucleus is the:
questions.explanation: Cyton (Soma) is the main cell body of a neurone.

questions.stem: In Practice Exam (Topic 5), Nissl's granules in cyton and dendrites consist of clumps of:
options: B) Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum and free Ribosomes
questions.answer: B) Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum and free Ribosomes
questions.explanation: Nissl's granules are RER and free ribosomes synthesizing protein.

questions.stem: In Practice Exam (Topic 5), Nissl's granules are strictly ABSENT in:
questions.explanation: Nissl's granules are absent in axon hillock and axon.

questions.stem: In Practice Exam (Topic 5), saltatory nerve impulse propagation leaps along myelinated axons at:
questions.explanation: Action potentials jump from Node of Ranvier to Node of Ranvier.

questions.stem: In Practice Exam (Topic 5), which CNS neuroglia construct the Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB)?
questions.explanation: Astrocytes form perivascular end-feet creating the Blood-Brain Barrier.

questions.stem: In Practice Exam (Topic 5), myelin sheath in the Central Nervous System (CNS) is synthesized by:
questions.explanation: Oligodendrocytes form CNS myelin; Schwann cells form PNS myelin.

questions.stem: In Practice Exam (Topic 5), phagocytic macrophage defense neuroglia in the CNS are:
questions.explanation: Microglia act as tissue macrophages defending the CNS.

questions.stem: In Practice Exam (Topic 5 - MSQ), select all neuroglial cells residing in the Central Nervous System (CNS): (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: CNS neuroglia: Astrocytes, Oligodendrocytes, Microglia, Ependymal. Schwann = PNS.

questions.stem: In Practice Exam (Topic 5 - MSQ), select all neuroglial cells residing in the Peripheral Nervous System (PNS): (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: PNS neuroglia include Schwann cells and Satellite cells.

questions.stem: In Practice Exam (Topic 5 - MSQ), select all anatomical locations containing Bipolar Neurones: (Select all that apply)
options: C) Inner ear vestibular and cochlear organs
answers: C) Inner ear vestibular and cochlear organs
questions.explanation: Bipolar neurones occur in retina, olfactory mucosa, and inner ear.
